_readme: Docs past the staleness threshold that have a RECORDED DECISION instead of a fix.
Two honest states, and the difference matters:
verified_current — somebody READ it and the content is still true. Say what you checked.
pending_review   — its subject still exists so the doc is plausibly fine, but NOBODY HAS
READ IT. Carries a review_by deadline; the test fails when it passes.
Conflating the two is how an unread document becomes an endorsed one.
When review happens: archiving is usually the right move — a doc that no longer describes
the system is worse than no doc, because it is discoverable and confident. If it must be
brought current, read-then-WRITE the whole file; an edit keeps the old structure and
strands every reference to what it changed.

docs/architecture/SENTINEL_CONSTITUTION..reason: Read in full on 2026-10-12. Principles I and III-IX still describe the code (phase-aware calibration, earned autonomy, honest over accurate, fail-open measurement, human authority). Principle II (measurement opacity: the system prompt must not expose scoring mechanics) is in tension with the current lean system prompt, which publishes the work_type calibration weights and frames measurement as collaborative; whether II stands, is amended, or the prompt is wrong is David's ruling, not edited here. Authors are David and Claude Code, so the principles are not rewritten unasked. Further check 2026-10-13: the work_type weights have been in the agent-facing lean system prompt since commit d106cd0c3 (2026-04-13, five weeks after this document) and in the public guide docs/human/end-users/05_EPISTEMIC_VECTORS_EXPLAINED.md; no amendment decision was logged; SENTINEL_GATE_REFERENCE.md line 5 still cites Principle II as its audience rule; and CHECK ADVISORY messages with K/U thresholds now reach the model. The contradiction is three documents and two delivery channels wide, not one prompt line. Amend or reaffirm Principle II (David).
